assumptions: affine spectrum computed for N <= 40 by direct evaluation
SAT spectra for N <= 6 for all laws; model enumeration (limit 1000) for N <= 9 for the restricted laws; N = 10..12 solved for selected laws
falsification: A law (other than LD) whose SAT spectrum differs from its affine spectrum; a non-affine model of (xy)z = x(y(zz)) or (xy)z = x((yz)z); a model count different from the predicted root count.
hypothesis: H-C06-3 (bold): apart from left-distributivity, every law of the family has anchored spectrum equal to its affine spectrum for N <= 6. H-C06-4 (derived by hand): the anchored models of (xy)z = x(y(zz)) are exactly x*y = x + a*y + 1 with a^2 + a = 1 (mod N); predicted counts 1 (N=1), 1 (N=5), 2 (N=11), 0 for other N <= 12. H-C06-5 (derived by hand): (xy)z = x((yz)z) has exactly one anchored model for odd N and none for even N.
methodology: Evaluate every affine table for every a in Z_N; compare with SAT; enumerate all anchored models of restricted laws and test each for affinity (T[x][y] - x - 1 = a*y for a single a).
question: For the 382 laws of EXP-C06-03, does the anchored spectrum coincide with the set of N for which some affine table x*y = x + a*y + 1 (mod N) satisfies the law? Are all anchored models of the restricted-spectrum laws affine?
